name: What are the most common hidden costs in a backyard guest house?

mainEntity.name: What extra costs surprise homeowners after they start a backyard guest house project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What extra costs surprise homeowners after they start a backyard guest house project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common surprises are not the walls and roof; they are the site conditions and coordination items. In Los Angeles-area projects, hidden costs often come from utility relocation, sewer and water tie-ins, drainage corrections, paving repairs, landscape restoration, engineering revisions, and permit-related changes. If the lot has slope, poor access, or tight construction staging, labor costs can also rise quickly. Premium finishes and late design changes are another major source of overruns. The best protection is a detailed preconstruction review that identifies the site constraints before the bid is finalized. Homeowners should ask for allowances, exclusions, and contingency percentages in writing so the budget reflects real conditions instead of ideal assumptions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden costs often include surveying, soils reports, utility trenching, demolition, grading, drainage, retaining walls, fire upgrades, and finish changes. On constrained Los Angeles lots, site work can cost as much as the structure itself. A realistic contingency is essential because small site issues can create large budget swings.
